number.why: The source explicitly reports RR 0.33 (95% CI 0.1-1.06) for AAD comparing probiotic with placebo, and states intention-to-treat analysis. The separate any-diarrhoea result is RR 0.45. As the ruling acknowledges, the explicit follow-up window belongs to any diarrhoea; an AAD-specific study-end timepoint is not independently established.

quotes.span: Three (2.5%) children in the probiotic group developed AAD (diarrhoea caused by Clostridium difficile or otherwise unexplained diarrhoea) compared to nine (7.5%) in the placebo group (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.1-1.06).
Analyses were by intention to treat.

Any diarrhoea (>or=3 loose or watery stools/day for >or=48 h occurring during or up to 2 weeks after the antibiotic therapy) occurred in nine (7.5%) patients in the probiotic group and in 20 (17%) patients in the placebo group (relative risk, RR 0.45, 95% confidence interval, CI 0.2-0.9).

entry.why: Children receiving standard antibiotic treatment satisfy the question's entry population of patients receiving antibiotics. The trial compares adjunctive probiotic with placebo.

quotes.span: Children (aged 3 months to 14 years) with common infections were enrolled in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in which they received standard antibiotic treatment plus 2 x 10(10) colony forming units of a probiotic (n = 120) or a placebo (n = 120), administered orally twice daily throughout antibiotic treatment.

missed: No additional finding changes either ruling. The served endpoint-definition metadata describes any diarrhoea rather than the narrower AAD endpoint, as shown in the quoted results; it should not be treated as an exact definition of the confirmed AAD estimate.
